smbd_deltas: the smbd challenge rip and the nes rip are the same level. the smbd one is 140 columns and starts at what is column 16 here - all eleven of its solid blocks (seven firebar pivots and four lone ones), both roof stubs, every lava pit, the bridge, the axe and bowser sit exactly sixteen columns left of their nes cells, and a cell-by-cell diff of the 140 x 13 overlap comes out clean apart from tiles a flame or a sprite is drawn over. so nothing in 1-4 moved between smb1 and smbd, and columns 0-15 - the opening raised platform, its three descending steps and the first lava pit - are transcribed off the nes rip, which is the only one that draws them. the two rips do differ past the axe: the nes one draws the toad room's ceiling, its floor and its two sprites out to column 159, the smbd one stops the roof at 143 and shapes the room differently. the bible follows the nes rip and carries the whole room, so it is 160 columns and not the 152 an earlier pass cut it at - the eight columns that pass dropped are nothing but roof and floor, but they are what the ending needs: the camera's last view opens at 147 instead of 142, which puts the axe wall out of the picture and gives the retainer, mario and the sign over them a room to stand in ("toad_x" on the bridge entry). challenge mode's own additions, five red coins and the yoshi egg replacing the ladder's top-middle coin, are recorded in "smbd" and are not compiled.
confidence_notes:
1-4 is transcribed cell by cell from the two map rips above, the way 1-1, 1-2 and 1-3 were: every 16x16 cell of both images was hashed and classified against a tile sheet cut from the same image (75 distinct tiles across the nes rip's 158 level columns, 63 across the smbd rip's 140), the two classifications were diffed column by column, and they agree everywhere they overlap (see smbd_deltas). the nes rip is grid-aligned with no offset - image row 13 is the ground row this schema names - and its columns 160-207 are the ripper's caption and legend, not level: the roof's mortar and the floor's both run unbroken to the last pixel of column 159 and there is not a cell of masonry past it. the smbd rip is offset sixteen columns right and one row down and carries no grid row 0, which holds nothing but sky.

the firebar count is measured and settles what the prose pass guessed at: the rips draw eleven of the castle's lone solid blocks and exactly seven of them carry a flame chain, which is the seven mariowiki names. the two rips caught the bars at different angles (the nes one diagonal, the smbd one straight down) yet the same seven have bars and the same four do not, so the four are blocks and not bars whose chain happened to be hidden inside masonry. each drawn chain reaches three cells from its pivot, which is six segments at the 8 px spacing hazards.c uses, so every "length": 6 is measured.

what is not measured: each bar's rotation speed and direction. a still frame cannot show either. all seven are written "slow" (physics.json's 0x28) because smb1's fast bar is a later-castle object, and six are written "cw" against one "ccw" at 88/4 - the nes rip has six bars at the same down-right angle and that one at its exact mirror, which is what two bars turning opposite ways from a shared phase look like, but which of the two senses is the clockwise one is a coin flip. speed and direction are therefore the level's one "approx" pair even though the entries carry a measured pivot.

the prose pass got two things wrong that the rips settle: the six coins before bowser are hidden blocks in two ranks of three, not a row of six, and the level has four lava pits, not the one the prose named. and the cell-by-cell pass got one thing wrong that a closer look at the same rip settles back the other way. it classified the 32x8 object at 138-139/6 as a bowser fireball in flight and wrote the bridge gap "lift": false on that reading. it is a lift. the plate's own pixels, read out of the nes rip a row at a time, are a white top edge, a solid red band, four repeats of an 8 px orange plate carrying a dark stud, an orange row and a red bottom edge - a straight-edged 32 px deck. the flame the same rip catches at 127/8 is 24x8, has no straight edge in it at all and is a tapered wavy tongue of dark red around an orange core. the two share only a palette. so the deck is restored as a measured lift_platform at row 6 with an approx travel (see the entry), and the gap keeps "lift": false for the other reason it was ever wanted: the compiler's wide-castle-gap rule must not throw a second, guessed deck across a pit the rips measured.

the engine's own compromises, all of them documented rather than hidden: the ground rows 13-14 are castle masonry in the rip and are stamped as such here, so the level has no BLOCK_GROUND cell at all; the four pits are still written as gap runs, because gap is the primitive that fills a castle pit with lava. hazards.c runs one shared spin phase per rate rather than one accumulator per bar, so two bars of the same rate and handedness always point the same way; m21 made every bar whose sweep can reach the view live, drawn and able to burn, so the pair at 84 and 88 - four columns apart - both turn and both burn, and the draw is capped at two full bars nearest the camera centre. and bowser's patrol runs from his measured cell out to the bridge's last column, which keeps him over the deck; the rip catches him at one instant and cannot show how far he paces.
